title: Make one folder match another, with a dry run first
summary: Copies new and changed files from a source folder to a destination folder so the destination matches the source. A dry run first lists what would be copied or deleted without changing anything. Deleting extra files happens only with the delete option.

aliases.text: sync two folders dry run first
rsync compare two folders dry run
make backup folder same as source
mirror a folder with rsync and delete extra files
compare two directories linux before copy
сравнить две папки перед копированием rsync
сделать папку копии такой же как исходная
зеркало папки rsync удалить лишние файлы

steps.explain: Dry run: show what would be copied, and with --delete also what would be removed from the destination. -n changes nothing. The slash after the source means copy its contents, not the folder itself.
steps.expect: File names to copy, lines starting with deleting for extra files, then a summary ending in (DRY RUN).

placeholders.name: SRC_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder that holds the correct files

placeholders.name: DST_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder to make match the source

alternatives.explain: Copy only: new and changed files are copied, but nothing in the destination is removed.
alternatives.expect: Only the files that would be copied.

steps.explain: Apply the same sync for real. Files in the destination that are not in the source are deleted.
steps.expect: sending incremental file list, then a summary with total size. No DRY RUN text.

alternatives.explain: Copy only, without deleting anything in the destination.

steps.explain: Run the dry run again. If the folders match, only the summary lines appear and no file names.
steps.expect: Only the summary, with no file names.

prerequisites: The destination folder exists; create it with mkdir -p if it does not

rollback.explain: Files removed by --delete cannot be recovered by rsync. Restore them from another copy or a backup. Keep a copy of the destination first if it holds data you cannot rebuild.

warnings: --delete removes files from the destination that are missing in the source. Read every deleting line in the dry run.
Swapping the source and the destination reverses the direction and can delete the files you wanted to keep.
